Job-market sweep for Prabhavit Gupta, a Venice-based AI/automation engineer. Today is 5 August 2026. Two previous sweeps have already covered the obvious ground, so your value is in the vocabulary and hosts they did NOT touch.

## Candidate profile (never invent beyond this)
- ~3 years experience across eight European companies (UK, Spain, France, Italy, Germany, Luxembourg, Netherlands), mostly freelance/collaborator engagements.
- **Indian passport, Italian EU long-term residence permit** -> no sponsorship needed anywhere in the EU. NOT UK, Swiss or US authorised.
- Venice-based. **Confirmed open to: remote-from-Venice, remote-within-Germany roles, office-based in an EU city, and Spain.** Do not down-score EU relocation any more.
- Stack: n8n (deep), TypeScript/JavaScript, Next.js, React, Node, PHP/Laravel, Supabase/PostgreSQL, Playwright, Claude Code, OpenAI + Anthropic APIs, Eden AI, Make.com/Zapier/Tray.ai, RAG, LLM agents with human-in-the-loop, Docker, AWS basics. Certifications: Microsoft Copilot Studio Agent Academy, Microsoft AI agents, Power Automate, Tray.ai Build Practitioner.
- Flagship: FlowSpace (Mar 2024 to ongoing) - grew platform 2,000 to 4,500+ users, led Bubble.io to Next.js + Laravel migration on a live product, built AI support agents, CRM lead capture and enrichment, GTM/outbound automations, scraping/parsing pipeline. Integrations: Office RnD, Nexudus, Clubee, Sendgrid, Google APIs.
- **No GitHub. No CS degree** (BA Philosophy/International Studies/Economics, Ca' Foscari Venice). No Java, no Go/Rust, no Python backend depth, no Kubernetes, no WordPress, no ML research. English only, Italian beginner and studying.
- Salary target EUR 30,000-40,000. Contract EUR 200/day. Sole trader on an Italian Partita IVA (NOT a limited company - clients who require an LTD/SRL are dead ends).

## Your slice: titles and hosts nobody has swept yet
**Titles already swept to death (do NOT repeat):** AI Engineer, Applied AI Engineer, AI Automation Engineer, Automations Engineer, Agent Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Engineer, Implementation Engineer, Deployment Engineer, Customer Engineer, GTM Engineer, Growth Engineer, MarTech Engineer, Revenue Operations Engineer, Full-Stack Engineer, Product Engineer, Founding Engineer, Technical Product Manager.

**Sweep these instead:**
"Integration Engineer", "Integrations Engineer", "Technical Account Manager", "Developer Advocate", "Developer Relations Engineer", "Technical Support Engineer", "Escalation Engineer", "Professional Services Engineer", "Delivery Engineer", "Automation Consultant", "AI Implementation Consultant", "Workflow Engineer", "Conversation Designer", "Solutions Architect (mid-level)", "Technical Consultant", "Internal Tools Engineer", "Business Automation Developer", "Low-code Developer", "Copilot Studio developer", "Power Automate developer".

That last cluster matters: he holds Microsoft Copilot Studio and Power Automate certifications and nobody has searched for those.

**Hosts nobody has swept:** use WebSearch `allowed_domains` (it is a hard filter) on `jobs.recruitee.com`, `careers.recruitee.com`, `jobs.teamtailor.com`, `apply.jobvite.com`, `breezy.hr`, `jobicy.com`, `remotive.com`, `nodesk.co`, `himalayas.app`, `arbeitnow.com`, `wellfound.com`, `jobs.workable.com` (the `jobs.` host renders; `apply.workable.com` does not), `jobs.personio.com`, `jobs.smartrecruiters.com`, `jobs.eu.lever.co`.

**Bias hard toward postings dated within the last 21 days.**

## Verification is the whole job
Fetch-based verification failed badly last time: four of the highest-scoring finds were listed as live by `api.ashbyhq.com` and returned "Job not found" the second a real browser opened them. So:
- WebFetch every posting URL and confirm it renders as ONE live posting, not a board index.
- Dead signatures: "Job not found"; a URL serving many jobs on one page; "no longer active"; a passed deadline.
- **State your confidence explicitly per row** and say what you actually saw. A title in page metadata is not proof of life.

## Exclusion list - already applied to, closed, gated or logged. NEVER report these again:
Arize AI, Arkipel, Attio, Ben, Bullpen Talent, Camunda, Checkly, Codex, Cohere, Cresta, Dash0, Duvo, EggAI, ElevenLabs, Eneba, Filigran, Fueled, G2i, GRAI, GTM Base, Gensyn, Glacis AI, Goldsky, HiPeople, Jamie, JobLeads, Kairos, Lovable, Mercura, Mindrift, Toloka AI, Moneyfarm, Musixmatch, MyEdSpace, Novosafe, Nuitee, Oh, OpenHands, Parloa, Pinnipedia, Quadrivia, Reedsy, Reflow, Remote People, Runpod, SalesCaptain, Satispay, Shippeo, Sourcegraph, Supabase, The Flex, The Global Talent Co, Unframe, Viktor, YLD, Zapier, dexter health, n8n, neptune.ai, peopleIX, Laioutr, salesHAX, RevOS, cargovibe, KFS GROUP, tem, Nearform, Aircall, Always Friday, Outliant, ClickHouse, Twilio, Neural Earth, Atmen, MAIA, alago, Stackgini, Cognite, GitLab, Hightouch, Firecrawl, Encord, Ophelos, Nooks, Exa, Roger, Jobgether, ZOE, Pragmatike, Starbridge, supermodular.ai, Platform Venture Studio.

## Scoring (total 100)
role match 30 + eligibility and work basis 25 + stack overlap 20 + seniority realism 15 + signal quality 10. Kill most of the 25 for UK/Swiss/US authorisation requirements or a non-EU office. Do NOT penalise EU relocation. Penalise talent marketplaces with no named end client on signal quality.

## Output - return this and nothing else
One block per role scoring 55+:

### <score> - <role title> · <company>
- **Where:** <verbatim location/eligibility sentence> · Tier 1 (workable from Venice today) / 2 (EU but a move) / 3 (outside the EU or needs authorisation he lacks) · Employee or Contract
- **Pay:** <figures or "not disclosed"> · **Posted:** <date or "not stated">
- **Why:** two or three sentences tied to specific things he has actually done.
- **Watch-outs:** the honest gaps, named.
- **Apply:** <canonical application URL>
- **Verified:** <what you fetched, what you saw, and your confidence>

Then a short "dead or unverifiable" list and the queries you ran. No preamble.

{"method":"project_read","path":"claude/application-rules.md","content":"# Standing rules for submitting applications on Prabhavit's behalf

These are his instructions, not suggestions, and several of them exist because they were got
wrong once already. Read this file before touching a single form. If a rule here conflicts with
your own judgement about what would "look better" to an employer, the rule wins — it's his
career and his call.

## The non-negotiables

1. **Attach the CV to every application. Never submit one without it.** Use only the CV file he
   most recently supplied — the exact PDF, unmodified. Do not regenerate it, reformat it, or
   substitute a version you made. If the file isn't available in this session, stop and ask;
   don't proceed with a CV-less application.

2. **Salary or rate expectation: €30,000–40,000.** Write it plainly — "€30,000–40,000" or
   "EUR 30,000–40,000, negotiable" at most. **Do not** pad it with explanations about market
   bands, do not substitute a higher figure because the posting advertises more, and do not
   write a paragraph where a number was asked for. If you think his number is low, say so once
   in chat and then use his number anyway.

3. **Never leave a cover letter field blank when one is asked for.** Adapt his motivation letter
   (`assets/motivation-letter.md`) to the specific role. Where the form takes a file, generate a
   PDF; where it takes text, paste the adapted body.

4. **When a form asks for years of experience and wants 3 or more, write 3.** Don't skip an
   application because a year count is above his. Answer honestly with 3 and let the employer
   decide. Same principle for any "do you have N years of X" free-text field: give the true
   number and one clause of context, no more.

5. **Skip join.com** unless he has signed in on that browser. Their apply flow forces account
   creation or Google sign-in, and account creation is off-limits.

6. **Don't make the writing sound AI-generated.** Details in the writing section below.

## His details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | Prabhavit Gupta (preferred: Prabhavit) |
| Email | prabhavitg@gmail.com |
| Phone | +39 351 610 7807 (country: Italy, +39) |
| Address | Via Zanetti, 10 · Venice · Veneto · 30175 · Italy |
| Location for city pickers | Venice, Venezia, Italy |
| LinkedIn | https://www.linkedin.com/in/prabhavit/ |
| GitHub / portfolio | none supplied — leave blank rather than inventing one |
| Work authorisation | Italian EU long-term residence permit. **Needs no sponsorship anywhere in the EU.** Not UK, Swiss or US authorisation. |
| Availability | Immediately — the FlowSpace contract ended July 2026 |
| Languages | English professional, Hindi native, Italian beginner |

Standard answers to the questions that recur:

- *Legally eligible to work where you'll work from?* → **Yes**
- *Which status allows you to work there?* → **citizen / permanent resident** (the EU long-term permit)
- *Will you require sponsorship now or in future?* → **No** for EU-based and remote-from-Italy roles. For a **UK, Swiss or US** role, the honest answer is **Yes** — answer it truthfully and flag the role to him rather than fudging it.
- *Able and willing to work remotely?* → **Yes**
- *Based in Europe?* → **Yes**
- *Previously worked in a customer-facing capacity?* → **Yes** (FlowSpace: mediated between the internal team, an external agency and members; Urlink: project manager on client requirements)
- *Production experience at a large enterprise (1,000+)?* → **"only shipped in smaller companies or startups"** — true, don't inflate it
- *AI agents / agentic workflows?* → **"built and operated agentic systems in production, including testing for non-determinism and failure recovery"** — true, and his strongest answer on any form
- *BPMN specifically?* → he has n8n workflow automation in production but no BPMN. Pick the middle option where one exists; never claim BPMN production experience
- *Native English speaker?* → **No, fluent at C2 level**
- *Pronouns, gender, ethnicity, disability, veteran status* → leave blank or "prefer not to say". Never guess demographic data.
- *How did you hear about us?* → the honest answer is a job board; pick "Job Board" / "Other" and say "job board" if a follow-up field appears.

## Writing that doesn't read as machine-written

His own motivation letter is the voice to match: direct, concrete, slightly formal, first person,
specific numbers, no salesmanship. Things to avoid because they are the tells:

- Openings like "I'm excited to apply" or "I am thrilled by the opportunity".
- Three-item lists everywhere, and sentences of identical length stacked together.
- "Leverage", "passionate about", "cutting-edge", "seamlessly", "robust solutions", "I thrive in".
- Restating the job description back at them instead of saying what he did.
- Perfect symmetry. Real writing has a short sentence after a long one, and occasionally starts with "But" or "So".

What to do instead: name the specific thing he built, the tool he built it in, and the number it
moved. Say plainly where he's weaker rather than papering over it — a sentence like "my agent work
has been in n8n rather than a Python harness, so I'd be learning your idioms early on" reads as
human and costs nothing.

## The facts worth reaching for

Use these rather than adjectives. They're all on his CV.

- FlowSpace: took over an existing system, grew the platform **2,000 → 4,500+ users**, led the migration from **Bubble.io to Next.js + Laravel** on a live product, built the support **AI agents**, lead capture and enrichment into the CRM, GTM and outbound automations, and a scraping/parsing tool that increased listings.
- Integrations shipped: **Office RnD, Nexudus** (automated bookings), Clubee API, Sendgrid, Google APIs, OpenAI/Anthropic, Eden AI.
- UltraStrategy: **CV-parsing tool in n8n + Eden AI**. Get2Germany: Google API tracking, AI tools for finding courses and jobs. Clubee: API integration, unit testing and QA.
- Urlink: built a platform largely with AI, acting as PM and developer.
- Eight European companies in about three years (UK, Spain, France, Italy, Germany, Luxembourg, Netherlands) — the ramp-fast argument.
- Certifications: Microsoft Copilot Studio Agent Academy, Microsoft AI agents, Power Automate, Tray.ai Build Practitioner.
- Degree: BA Philosophy, International Studies & Economics, Ca' Foscari Venice. No CS degree — don't hide it, don't apologise for it.

## Things you must not do

- Create an account, set a password, or sign in as him.
- Solve a CAPTCHA.
- Enter payment details, government ID numbers, or a date of birth he hasn't given.
- Invent a GitHub link, a portfolio URL, a referral name, or demographic data.
- Claim experience he can't evidence — specifically BPMN, Python backend depth, ML research, or a language beyond English.
- Submit two applications to the same company for roles he clearly doesn't qualify for. One good application beats two scattershot ones.

When you hit one of these, stop that application, leave the form filled if you can, and tell him
exactly what's needed.

## Log every submission

After each one, record: company, role, the ATS, what was entered in each non-obvious field, the
confirmation text you actually saw, and the link. If you didn't see a confirmation, it didn't
happen — say so. He is tracking this in a spreadsheet and a silent failure is worse than a
visible one.

Our story:

Every year millions of people are either filing their taxes in fear or giving up on their tax refund altogether. We're working on fixing that. Our intuitive app enables anyone, regardless of education or background, to file their taxes with newfound confidence.

Spread across Germany, Spain and the UK, the team at Taxfix Group with its brands Taxfix and Steuerbot, is a compassionate group of solution-finders. We speak our minds openly, and with over 400 professionals, including tax experts, developers, and IT security experts, we're rich in ideas and voices. The group has facilitated more than 3.5 billion euros in tax refunds for its customers since its founding in 2016.

The opportunity:

We’re looking for a Content Engineer to join our Organic Acquisition team. This is not a traditional content role - you won’t be writing blog posts or landing pages. We have an excellent agency partner handling content production across DE, UK, and ES.

Instead, you’ll be the person who builds the systems, automations, and workflows that make our content operations scale across three markets. You’ll design and run CRO and ASO experiments with proper rigor, automate structured content pipelines, and create cross-market templates that eliminate repetitive manual work.

Your playground: a proven multi-market organic acquisition engine with real room to systematise, automate, and experiment - using AI-powered tools and no-code automation platforms to move at a pace that compounds.

Your responsibilities and decisions:

CRO, ASO & Personalisation Experimentation

Design, execute, and analyse conversion rate optimisation experiments across web and app store listings

Build and own a structured experimentation framework: hypothesis → prioritisation → execution → measurement → learning

Design and implement multi-armed bandit testing to continuously optimise content variants across segments and markets

Drive content personalisation for key user segments (e.g., tax classes, employment types, filing interests) to improve relevance and conversion

Work with our ASO agency and tooling (Peec.ai) to improve experiment quality and velocity; own the experimentation process end-to-end

Document experiment results and build a searchable knowledge base of learnings that compounds over time

Content Automation & Structured Data

Build automated workflows using no-code/low-code tools (n8n, Make) and AI tools (Claude, Langdock, Antigravity)

Automate structured content generation beyond FAQs - including HowTo, Article, TaxCalculator, Breadcrumb, and Q&A schema, as well as emerging formats optimised for AI answer engines (AEO) and LLM consumption.

Define and maintain scalable content templates for diverse content types: comparison pages, how-to guides, tax topic explainers, calculators, and editorial formats

Create translation automation pipelines that work across DE, EN, and ES content

Design and roll out cross-market content templates that can be localized efficiently without manual duplication

Content Operations & Tooling

Identify manual, repetitive processes in our content workflow and systematically automate them

Work daily with our content and SEO stack: Uniform (CMS), Ahrefs, Peec.ai (ASO), Google Search Console, and Google Analytics

Leverage our AI tooling stack - Langdock, Antigravity, Claude (Code) - to accelerate content operations and experimentation

Build and maintain dashboards to track content performance and experiment results

Manage the interface between our content agency and internal systems to ensure seamless handoffs

Ensure content quality and consistency across all three markets through automated checks and validation

Your profile:

2–4 years of experience in content operations, growth marketing, or a similar role at a digital product company

Hands-on proficiency with automation platforms: n8n, Make, or similar - you can build workflows independently without engineering support

Strong working knowledge of AI tools and how to use them productively: Claude, AI agents, MCPs, custom skills

Experience designing and running structured experiments (A/B tests, multivariate tests, multi-armed bandits) with proper statistical rigor

Understanding of ASO and/or CRO fundamentals - you know what moves the needle in app stores and on landing pages

Understanding of structured data formats (JSON-LD, schema.org markup) and how search engines and LLMs consume content

Experience with or strong interest in content personalisation across user segments

Familiarity with CMS platforms (ideally headless/composable like Uniform) and SEO tooling (Ahrefs, Search Console)

High ownership mindset - you drive problems to resolution without waiting to be directed

Full professional proficiency in English; German and/or Spanish are a bonus but not required

Nice-to-haves:

Basic scripting skills (Python, JavaScript) - not required, but it opens doors

Experience with AEO tooling (Peec.ai or similar)

Experience in a multi-market content setup

Background in fintech or tax-related products

Why Taxfix?

A chance to do meaningful, people-centric work with an international team of passionate professionals.

Holistic well-being with free mental health coaching sessions and yoga.

A monthly allowance to spend on an extensive range of services that you can use and roll over as flexibly as you like.

Employee stock options for all employees - because everyone deserves to benefit from the success they help to create.

30 annual vacation days and flexible working hours.

A generous learning budget to support your personal and professional development and guidance from our internal L&D experts.

Work from abroad for up to six weeks every year. Just align with your team, and then enjoy your trip.

Plenty of opportunities to socialise as a team. In addition to internal meetups, our international team hosts regular get-togethers - virtually and in person when possible.

Free tax declaration filing, of course, through the Taxfix app - and internal support for all personal tax-related questions.

Have a four-legged friend in your life? We’re happy to have dogs join us in the office.

Excited? So are we. Learn more about Team Taxfix on our blog and get a glimpse of our culture.

At Taxfix, we believe that incredible things happen when you have a wealth of perspectives and experiences. We're proudly committed to equal employment and development opportunities no matter your gender, race, religion, age, sexual orientation, colour, disability, or place of origin. To help mitigate any potential unconscious biases, we ask that you refrain from including your picture, age, or marital status on your CV. Let your experiences speak for themselves.

Our story:

Every year millions of people are either filing their taxes in fear or giving up on their tax refund altogether. We're working on fixing that. Our intuitive app enables anyone, regardless of education or background, to file their taxes with newfound confidence.

Spread across Germany, Spain and the UK, the team at Taxfix Group with its brands Taxfix and Steuerbot, is a compassionate group of solution-finders. We speak our minds openly, and with over 400 professionals, including tax experts, developers, and IT security experts, we're rich in ideas and voices. The group has facilitated more than 3.5 billion euros in tax refunds for its customers since its founding in 2016.

About the role

Across marketing - steering, paid channel operations, creative production, experimentation, reporting - skilled people still spend days on work that follows a pattern. That was just the cost of doing business until coding agents arrived and dropped the speed limit for building internal software from months to days. The tools to erase that repetitive work now exist, and most of the gain hasn’t been claimed yet.

You claim it. This is a founding-engineer role for the automation layer of our marketing operating system. Taxfix’s marketing team is rebuilding around an agentic-first way of working, where AI is the default mode for all work - and you build the systems that make it real: agent harnesses, data and context pipelines, integrations, and internal tooling.

You embed with our teams, find the workflows that eat the most time or cap the most output, and remove them. You choose what to build, you build it, you ship it, and you run it.

What you'll do

Design and build our agentic operating model. Taxfix is rebuilding around an AI-first, agentic-first way of working, and you drive or contribute to what that operating system becomes. Understand the problem space and the solution space, map how the work should run when agents carry the load, then design the system and build it.

Find the bottlenecks, then remove them. Embed with the Creative Studio, User Acquisition, CRM, SEO/AEO, and analytics teams. Map how work actually flows, find where hours disappear or quality caps out, and turn multi-day processes into effective automated systems.

Build advanced agentic systems, including agent harnesses. Go past single-shot scripts and one-step automations. Design and build the agent harnesses that let agents run complex, multi-step workflows toward a goal: the orchestration, the tool interfaces, the guardrails, the memory, and the evaluation loops that keep them reliable. Example targets: automate creative production workflows or build a multi-agent system to automate channel operations end-to-end.

Own your architecture. Build software where we don't buy it. Wire up a lean no-code stack where that wins. You decide based on ROI for the use case, then handle your own deployment, DevOps, and maintenance.

Systematize and scale what works. Recognize patterns across teams. When you automate a workflow for one, abstract and modularize it so the rest of the org can run and benefit from it. Document the tools and the playbooks so the wins compound over time.

Turn individuals into builders. As you ship, you pull marketers up with you: hand off tools they can run and extend, show them how you built it, and contribute to our move toward an AI-first organization. You lead this shift by building and coaching others.

Who you are

The 33/33/33 hybrid. You work at the intersection of marketing, engineering, and analytics: about a third marketing sense, a third software engineering or advanced marketing automation, a third analytics and data. Few people carry all three. You are one of them, or you are close and hungry to close the gap.

We hire from two directions and weight them equally:

A (former) software engineer who wants to work on marketing and growth problems, or

A marketing-automation or MarTech builder with real full-stack engineering range.

Either way, you build. You have shipped systems, not only configured them.

High agency & low ego. You are a self-starter. You get close to teams, understand the opportunity, and implement it end to end. You set your own success metrics around the efficiency and output you unlock.

Comfortable in the ambiguity. You build the infrastructure, choose the tools, deploy the software, and maintain it, with no map or backlog handed to you. You read this as the appeal, not as a risk.

High conscientiousness and relentless curiosity. You finish what you start and hold the bar high on the work that ships. And you are genuinely obsessed with where AI is going: you are the first to dig into a new capability, figure out how it works, and ask what it means for our work. That curiosity extends across the full Growth area, where marketing, product, engineering, data, and design meet.

A track record of building internal tools, automation pipelines, or backend integrations that changed how real work got done. Software engineering, MarTech, or marketing automation backgrounds all qualify.

Hands-on experience with modern AI-assisted build tools (Claude Code, agent frameworks, model APIs) used to ship working software fast.

Fluency with REST APIs, webhooks, data pipelines, and connecting disparate software platforms (e.g. creative suites, ad network APIs, CRM systems)

Solid grounding in analytics and data management, knowing how data flows through internal systems to power automated marketing operations.
